question: Articles 21 and 22 TEU provide that it is for the Council to define the strategic interests and objectives of the Union’s external action.

As regards the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP), implementation and external representation are, in principle, the responsibility of the High Representative (Article 27 TEU), whilst the Commission President, in accordance with Article 17 TEU, represents the Commission in matters falling within her own competences.

In practice, there is often an overlapping or unclear division of roles, including in the context of the so-called ‘Team Europe’ approach, whereby the Commission President also adopts external political positions vis-à-vis third countries.
This situation raises questions about the division of competences in the field of the Union’s external action between the Commission President, the Council and the High Representative. 1.

How does the Commission interpret the division of competences under the Treaty in the field of the CFSP between the Commission President (Article 17 TEU) and the High Representative (Article 27 TEU) when it comes to public or diplomatic positions vis-àvis third countries?

What safeguards are in place to ensure that, in external contacts, the Commission President does not adopt positions on matters falling within the exclusive competence of the Council in the field of the CFSP?
To what extent does the ‘Team Europe’ approach affect the division of roles between the Commission President, the High Representative and the Council with regard to the Union’s external action?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.5.2026) 1. and 2. The general provisions on the Union’s external action in the Treaty on European Union provide that the Union shall ensure consistency between the different areas of its external action1. The Council and the Commission, assisted by the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, cooperate to that effect.

This is without prejudice to the fact that, with the exception of the Common Foreign and Security Policy, it is for the Commission to ensure the external representation of the Union2. 3. The Team Europe approach focuses on joining forces, delivering more effectively, increasing global impact and avoiding duplication of efforts, while respecting the division of competences under the Treaties.

It aims at bringing together the European Union, its Member States — including their implementing agencies and public development banks — as well as the European Investment Bank and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
1 Article 21(3) of the Treaty on European Union. 2 Article 17(1) of the Treaty on European Union.
